The frame's rendering is the opening bytes of both sov-loop.js dispatches on the pristine tree.

The landing-gate half reads honestly: _observed_path takes the observation's location from the request rather than from a field inside the observation, and _root() closing the ledger leak is a real repair.
residuals: Five of the eight UNREACHABLE entries were wrong: each was reachable through audit.violations on legal, lexer-clean JavaScript, and each was a case nobody wrote recorded as a gate that does not exist. The register asserted lexer.unreadable refuses an unbalanced brace before any rule reads the function; it does not, because lexer masks strings while render._body and frames.blocks scanned raw source - which lexer.py's own comment in the same commit concedes.

derives_from_agent_result convicts 272 bindings on the pristine tree, including integer loop counters: `for (var i = 0; i < plan.operations.length; i++)` returns the whole init clause as what is written into i, so every name in the condition pollutes it. Inert today only because the decision path it feeds is empty on the shipped tree.

audit's frame guard tested the literal text `function witnessFrame(` while render.DECLARATIONS knows three shapes, so a const-declared frame made the frame rules skip and the identity rule switch itself off. Latent in the repo-wide predicate rather than a live gate defeat.
Two graders answer `does this file have a frame?` differently - one by literal text, one by DECLARATIONS - which is the shape of several defeats already in the corpus.
The three limits the account discloses reproduce as stated and are recorded rather than counted against the claim.
standing_reason: The work is real, self-tested, and lands its corpus; that establishes BUILT.
